title: The Vineyard Song
summary: The first-person narrator announces a song concerning his beloved’s vineyard on a fruitful hill. The song describes its preparation and its production of wild grapes despite the expectation of grapes.
locations: Unspecified narrative setting; a vineyard on a fruitful hill is described in the song

explicit_facts.text: The first-person narrator announces a song to his well-beloved concerning his beloved’s vineyard.
The well-beloved has a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.
He fenced it, removed its stones, planted the choicest vine, built a tower in its midst, and made a wine-press there.
He expected grapes, but the vineyard brought forth wild grapes.

unspecified_visual_details: The narrator’s appearance, surroundings, and audience are unspecified.
The well-beloved’s identity and appearance are unspecified.
The vineyard’s dimensions and the designs of its fence, tower, and wine-press are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And then will I sing to my well-beloved a song of my beloved, touching his vineyard.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

narration.text: and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The speaker label follows the task’s explicit identification of the first-person narrator as Nephi; these two verses do not themselves name him.
The vineyard’s preparation and yield are reported within the song, not present physical action around the narrator.
The supplied verses do not explain what the vineyard represents.
prohibited_inventions: Do not reenact the reported vineyard preparation or yield as a new present-tense scene.
Do not place Nephi physically in the vineyard or compress preparation and yield into one moment.
Do not assign the well-beloved a named or divine identity or invent a visible appearance.
Do not invent an audience, melody, performance setting, or additional dialogue.
Do not depict the vineyard imagery as a literal supernatural event.

title: Judge the Vineyard
summary: An address asks the inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah to judge between the speaker and the speaker's vineyard. The speaker asks what more could have been done for it and says it brought forth wild grapes instead of grapes.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker asks the inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Judah to judge between the speaker and the speaker's vineyard.
The speaker asks what more could have been done for the vineyard and says it brought forth wild grapes rather than the expected grapes.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
The physical setting and whether the people addressed are present.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, O inhabitants of Jerusalem, and men of Judah, judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unknown speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: What could have been done more to my vineyard that I have not done in it? Wherefore, when I looked that it should bring forth grapes it brought forth wild grapes.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unknown speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Although Nephi is identified as the chapter's first-person narrator, these verses do not identify the speaker of the vineyard address.
The vineyard language does not establish a visible event or physical setting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the speaker as Nephi or another named figure.
Do not stage the vineyard imagery as a literal event.
Do not depict the addressees as physically present without textual support.
Do not invent actions, responses, or additional dialogue.

title: What Will Be Done to the Vineyard
summary: An unidentified vineyard speaker announces the removal of the vineyard’s hedge and the breaking down of its wall, leaving it to be eaten up and trodden down. The speaker announces that the vineyard will be laid waste, neither pruned nor dug, overgrown with briers and thorns, and denied rain by a command to the clouds.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker announces that the vineyard’s hedge will be removed and it will be eaten up.
The speaker announces that the vineyard’s wall will be broken down and it will be trodden down.
The speaker announces that the vineyard will be laid waste, neither pruned nor dug, and overgrown with briers and thorns.
The speaker announces a command to the clouds that they rain no rain upon the vineyard.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Static vineyard, hedge, and wall imagery could illustrate the teaching without depicting the announced actions as occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s identity, appearance, and physical setting.
The vineyard’s location, layout, and appearance.
The materials and appearance of the hedge and wall.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up; and I will break down the wall thereof, and it shall be trodden down;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified vineyard speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: but there shall come up briers and thorns;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified vineyard speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: I will also command the clouds that they rain no rain upon it.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified vineyard speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Nephi’s role as chapter narrator does not identify him as the vineyard speaker in these verses.
The vineyard imagery is a teaching expressed through future announcements, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the vineyard speaker as Nephi or another named figure.
Do not depict the announced destruction, overgrowth, or withholding of rain as events currently occurring.
Do not invent a visible divine appearance, audience, physical setting, or additional dialogue.
Do not assign an interpretation or identity to the vineyard beyond the supplied text.

title: The Vineyard Identified
summary: The vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is identified as the house of Israel and the men of Judah as his pleasant plant. He looked for judgment and righteousness, but there was oppression and a cry.

explicit_facts.text: The vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his pleasant plant.
He looked for judgment and righteousness, but there was oppression and a cry.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visible people or location.

narration.text: For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant; and he looked for judgment, and behold, oppression; for righteousness, but behold, a cry.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vineyard language is explicitly interpreted in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not turn the metaphor into a literal scene of people transformed into plants.

title: House upon House
summary: A woe is declared against those who join house to house until no place remains. The Lord of Hosts foretells desolate houses and cities without inhabitants. Vineyard and seed yields are foretold to be small.

explicit_facts.text: A woe is declared against those who join house to house until there can be no place.
The Lord of Hosts says many houses shall be desolate and great and fair cities shall be without inhabitants.
Ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of a homer shall yield an ephah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Closely spaced houses could illustrate the warning without showing the foretold desolation as an event already occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The houses and their location are not described.
No visible appearance is given for the Lord of Hosts.

spoken_dialogue.text: of a truth many houses shall be desolate, and great and fair cities without inhabitant.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord of Hosts

narration.text: Wo unto them that join house to house, till there can be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!
Yea, ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and the seed of a homer shall yield an ephah.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The desolation and yields are foretold, not narrated as events occurring in the scene.
The Lord of Hosts is identified as a speaker, but no visible presence is established.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the foretold desolation or poor harvest as already occurring.
Do not give the Lord of Hosts an invented appearance.
Do not name a city or identify particular owners.

title: Feasting Without Regard
summary: A woe is pronounced against those who follow strong drink from morning until night. Their feasts include instruments and wine, but they do not regard the Lord's work.
characters: Unnamed people addressed by the warning

explicit_facts.text: The warning addresses people who rise early to follow strong drink, continue until night, and are inflamed by wine.
Their feasts include a harp, viol, tabret, pipe, and wine.
They do not regard the work of the Lord or consider the operation of his hands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Unnamed people at a feast with the listed instruments and wine.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's number, identities, clothing, and appearance.
The feast's physical setting and whether anyone plays the instruments.

narration.text: Wo unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink, that continue until night, and wine inflame them!
And the harp, and the viol, the tabret, and pipe, and wine are in their feasts; but they regard not the work of the Lord, neither consider the operation of his hands.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The woe is a warning, not a separately narrated event.
Do not depict the Lord or his hands as visibly present on the basis of this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names or biographies to the people at the feasts.
Do not invent a physical setting, divine appearance, or spoken dialogue.

title: Captivity and Thirst
summary: The people have gone into captivity because they have no knowledge; their honorable men are famished, and their multitude is dried up with thirst.

explicit_facts.text: The people have gone into captivity because they have no knowledge.
Their honorable men are famished, and their multitude is dried up with thirst.
The verse describes hell as enlarging and opening its mouth, and says the people's glory, multitude, pomp, and one who rejoices shall descend into it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The reported captivity, hunger, and thirst can be suggested without showing them unfolding as a new event.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, captors, and people's appearances are not specified.

narration.text: Therefore, my people are gone into captivity, because they have no knowledge; and their honorable men are famished, and their multitude dried up with thirst.
Therefore, hell hath enlarged herself, and opened her mouth without measure; and their glory, and their multitude, and their pomp, and he that rejoiceth, shall descend into it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Hell's enlarged mouth is figurative language, not a narrated visible creature or event.
The descent into hell is expressed as something that shall happen, not as an event already shown.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage the reported captivity as a newly occurring scene or invent captors.
Do not depict hell as a literal creature or show the future descent as a visible event.

title: The Lofty Humbled
summary: The passage foretells the humbling of the mean man, the mighty man, and the lofty; the exaltation of the Lord of Hosts and the sanctification of God; and lambs feeding while strangers eat the waste places of the fat ones.
locations: waste places of the fat ones

explicit_facts.text: The mean man shall be brought down, the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled.
The Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in judgment, and God that is holy shall be sanctified in righteousness.
Lambs shall feed after their manner, and strangers shall eat the waste places of the fat ones.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Lambs feeding could illustrate the future image in verse 17 without placing the statements in verses 15–16 in the same physical moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of any person or divine figure.
The precise appearance and location of the waste places.

narration.text: And the mean man shall be brought down, and the mighty man shall be humbled, and the eyes of the lofty shall be humbled.
But the Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in judgment,
Then shall the lambs feed after their manner, and the waste places of the fat ones shall strangers eat.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements, not a narrated sequence of simultaneous visible events.
The verses do not describe a visible appearance of the Lord of Hosts or God.
These verses do not identify their narrator as Nephi.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or invent a divine appearance.
Do not stage the humbling, judgment, and feeding as one simultaneous event.
Do not invent identities, dialogue, or a specific setting for the strangers.

title: Cords of Iniquity
summary: A woe is pronounced against those described as drawing iniquity with cords of vanity and sin with a cart rope. They call for the Holy One of Israel's work and counsel to come so they may see and know.
characters: Those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity

explicit_facts.text: A woe is pronounced against those described as drawing iniquity with cords of vanity and sin as with a cart rope.
Those people call for the work and counsel of the Holy One of Israel to come so they may see and know.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, number of people, and their appearances are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Let him make speed, hasten his work, that we may see it; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel draw nigh and come, that we may know it.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity

narration.text: Wo unto them that draw iniquity with cords of vanity, and sin as it were with a cart rope;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The cords and cart rope are figures of speech, not narrated physical action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict people literally hauling sin with ropes.
Do not depict the Holy One of Israel appearing or performing an action.

title: Woes Against Moral Reversal and Self-Regard
summary: Woes are pronounced against those who reverse moral judgments and sensory comparisons, and against those wise and prudent in their own sight.

explicit_facts.text: A woe is pronounced against those who call evil good and good evil, put darkness for light and light for darkness, and put bitter for sweet and sweet for bitter.
A woe is pronounced against those wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own sight.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visible people or setting.
Any symbolic imagery used to represent the teachings.

narration.text: Wo unto them that call evil good, and good evil, that put darkness for light, and light for darkness, that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!
Wo unto the wise in their own eyes and prudent in their own sight!

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparisons are teachings, not narrated literal transformations.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal transformations of light, darkness, sweetness, or bitterness.
Do not invent speakers, people, or events.

title: Woe Against Drink and Injustice
summary: A woe is pronounced against mighty drinkers and those who justify the wicked for reward and take righteousness away from the righteous.

explicit_facts.text: A woe is pronounced against the mighty to drink wine and men of strength to mingle strong drink.
The accused justify the wicked for reward and take away the righteousness of the righteous.

unspecified_visual_details: Whether any of the people described are shown.
The setting and appearance of any people shown.

narration.text: Wo unto the mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink;
Who justify the wicked for reward, and take away the righteousness of the righteous from him!

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses pronounce a woe; they do not narrate a specific drinking occasion or transaction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a court, a visible reward exchange, or named participants.

title: The Withering Root
summary: A warning compares destruction to fire consuming stubble and chaff and says their root shall be rottenness and their blossoms shall rise as dust because they rejected the Lord's law and word.

explicit_facts.text: Fire consuming stubble and flame consuming chaff are comparisons in the warning.
Their root shall be rottenness, and their blossoms shall go up as dust.
They have cast away the law of the Lord of Hosts and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of those described as “they.”
The setting of the warning.

narration.text: Therefore, as the fire devoureth the stubble, and the flame consumeth the chaff, their root shall be rottenness, and their blossoms shall go up as dust; because they have cast away the law of the Lord of Hosts, and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The fire comparison is a figure of speech, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal fire destroying people or crops.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord of Hosts or the Holy One of Israel.

title: Judgment Described
summary: The Lord is angry with his people and has smitten them. The hills tremble, and carcasses are torn in the streets. His anger remains.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord's anger is kindled against his people; he has stretched forth his hand against them and smitten them.
The hills tremble, and carcasses are torn in the midst of the streets.
His anger is not turned away, and his hand remains stretched out.

unspecified_visual_details: The people's identities and the means of the smiting.
The Lord's appearance, which the verse does not describe.
The appearance of the hills and streets.

narration.text: Therefore, is the anger of the Lord kindled against his people, and he hath stretched forth his hand against them, and hath smitten them;
and the hills did tremble, and their carcasses were torn in the midst of the streets.
For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse reports these events; do not restage them as a new present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show gore, blood, or severed body parts.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or depict a literal divine hand.
Do not invent the identities of the people or the means of the smiting.

title: The Future Ensign
summary: A future lifting of an ensign and summons to distant nations is described. They will come swiftly, without weariness, stumbling, or sleep; their girdles and shoe-latchets will remain intact.

explicit_facts.text: A figure referred to as “he” will lift up an ensign to distant nations and hiss to them from the end of the earth.
The nations will come swiftly; none will be weary or stumble.
None will slumber or sleep; their girdles will not be loosed, and their shoe-latchets will not be broken.

unspecified_visual_details: The identity and appearance of the figure referred to as “he”.
The identities, number, and appearance of the nations.
The ensign’s design and location.

narration.text: And he will lift up an ensign to the nations from far,
and will hiss unto them from the end of the earth;
and behold, they shall come with speed swiftly;
None shall slumber nor sleep;
neither shall the girdle of their loins be loosed, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage describes future events, not an approach already underway.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the figure referred to as “he” or the summoned nations.
Do not depict the predicted approach as a present event.
Do not invent an ensign design, leaders, or dialogue.

title: Arrows, Bows, and Roaring
summary: The verses describe sharp arrows, bent bows, horses’ hoofs, wheels, and roaring. They foretell that an unidentified group shall lay hold of prey and carry it away, with none to deliver.

explicit_facts.text: Their arrows shall be sharp and all their bows bent; their horses’ hoofs are compared to flint, their wheels to a whirlwind, and their roaring to a lion’s.
They shall roar like young lions, lay hold of prey, and carry it away safe; none shall deliver.

unspecified_visual_details: The group’s identity and appearance.
The prey’s identity.

narration.text: Whose arrows shall be sharp, and all their bows bent, and their horses’ hoofs shall be counted like flint, and their wheels like a whirlwind, their roaring like a lion.
They shall roar like young lions; yea, they shall roar, and lay hold of the prey, and shall carry away safe, and none shall deliver.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparisons to flint, a whirlwind, and lions are figures of speech, not literal transformations.
The verses describe what shall happen, not a present event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or name the group or the prey.

title: A Foretold Day of Darkness
summary: The verse foretells that in that day they shall roar against them like the sea. If they look toward the land, there will be darkness and sorrow, and the light will be darkened in its heavens.
locations: An unspecified land and its heavens, as described in the prophecy

explicit_facts.text: The verse foretells that in that day, unidentified parties shall roar against others like the roaring of the sea.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A darkened sky over an unspecified land could illustrate the foretold darkness without presenting it as a current event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearances of those referred to as “they” and “them.”
The identity and appearance of the land.
